affiliation: Universität Rostock, Institute of Physics (previously Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena, IAP, with S. Nolte)
glasses_used: fused silica (Corning 7980, high-purity, 10–15 cm long samples)
laser_systems:
Coherent RegA 9000 regenerative amplifier seeded by Mira Ti:sapphire oscillator; 800 nm, 150 fs, 100 kHz, 450 nJ; sample translated at 100 mm/min in 15 cm Corning 7980
Regenerative Ti:sapphire amplifier seeded by Mira 900; ~450 nJ at 100 kHz; NA 0.35 objective; 10 cm fused-silica samples
topics: Discrete optics and discrete solitons in fs-laser-written waveguide arrays, Photonic Floquet topological insulators (helical waveguides), Anomalous Floquet topological insulators, Supersymmetric optics / mode converters, Non-Hermitian and PT-symmetric photonic lattices
summary: Szameit's group writes evanescently coupled waveguide lattices in fused silica with a 100 kHz Ti:sapphire amplifier (RegA 9000) and uses them as a test bed for discrete, topological and non-Hermitian photonics. Key results include the first discrete solitons in fs-written arrays (2005), the photonic Floquet topological insulator (2013, with Segev/Rechtsman) and the anomalous Floquet insulator (2017). Our lab is linked to this group.

affiliation: The Pennsylvania State University, Department of Physics (Professor of Physics, Associate Head for Research)
topics: Topological photonics in fs-laser-written waveguide arrays (Floquet topological insulators), Topological solitons and nonlinear topological photonics in laser-written arrays (2021 talk abstract), Topological protection of photonic mid-gap defect modes (Nature Photonics 2018, listed on his profile), Light–structured-matter interaction in the quantum and nonlinear regimes
summary: Rechtsman, first author of the photonic Floquet topological insulator paper (Nature 2013, with Szameit and Segev), now runs a Penn State group that writes 'hundreds of waveguides' in glass by femtosecond direct laser writing (Azrieli profile). The group works on topological, nonlinear and quantum photonics in these arrays. According to a secondary source, recent work uses EAGLE XG borosilicate and a 1030 nm fiber laser.

affiliation: RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau, Department of Physics (Juniorprofessorin, W1); formerly Feodor Lynen postdoctoral fellow with M. C. Rechtsman at Penn State (from 01/03/2020)
topics: Waveguides and topological photonics (Humboldt profile keywords), Nonlinear photonics: fractional Thouless pumping of solitons (Nature Physics 2023, with Rechtsman), 3D micro-printing (two-photon direct laser writing), Orbital angular momentum modes in waveguides
summary: Christina Jörg, a former Penn State postdoc of Rechtsman (Humboldt/Feodor Lynen fellow), is now a junior professor at RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau. Her listed keywords are waveguides, topological photonics, nonlinear photonics, 3D micro-printing and orbital angular momentum. At Penn State she co-authored the Nature Physics 2023 paper on fractional Thouless pumping of solitons in laser-written arrays.

affiliation: Heriot-Watt University, School of Engineering and Physical Sciences (Institute of Photonics and Quantum Sciences), Nonlinear Optics group, Edinburgh
glasses_used: erbium-doped glasses (amplifiers/lasers; HW thesis record https://www.ros.hw.ac.uk/handle/10399/2325), Er-doped bismuthate glass (CW and mode-locked waveguide lasers; HW thesis record), bismuth-ion-doped silicate glass (Opt. Express 2006, Δn up to ~4.3e-3), chalcogenide glasses including GASIR-1 (HW thesis and research-portal records)
topics: Ultrafast laser inscription (ULI) of photonic devices, Waveguide amplifiers and lasers in doped glasses (Er, Er-bismuthate, Tm; mode-locked waveguide lasers), Mid-IR waveguides and waveguide lasers (chalcogenide GASIR-1; Tm-doped sesquioxide ceramic), ULI plus selective chemical etching for optofluidics and biophotonics (cell-sorting biochips), Ultrafast nonlinear optics, white-light continuum
summary: Kar leads the Nonlinear Optics group at Heriot-Watt and has more than 30 years in nonlinear optics (HW page). He is one of the main developers of ultrafast laser inscription: waveguide amplifiers and lasers in Er-, Er:bismuthate- and Bi-doped glasses, chalcogenide mid-IR waveguides, and ULI-plus-etching optofluidic chips.

affiliation: Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore, Department of Physics; collaborates with M. C. Rechtsman (Penn State)
laser_systems: Femtosecond fiber laser, 1030 nm (secondary: same 2024 supplementary)
topics: fs-laser-written waveguide lattices with synthetic magnetic flux via Floquet engineering (IISc project 2022–2024), Flat-band photonic lattices: excitation of compact localized states, Topological edge states and solitons in driven waveguide lattices (with Rechtsman)
summary: Mukherjee is PI of an Indian government-funded project at IISc Bangalore on fs-laser-written waveguide lattices with synthetic magnetic flux. A 2024 IISc/Penn State paper with Rechtsman describes arrays written in EAGLE XG with a 1030 nm fiber laser. He is the India-based fs-written glass-waveguide researcher closest to the Szameit/Rechtsman/Jörg circle.

affiliation: CNR – Istituto di Fotonica e Nanotecnologie (IFN), Milan, with Politecnico di Milano, Dipartimento di Fisica (A. Crespi)

summary: Osellame's group at CNR-IFN and Politecnico di Milano is a leading fs-laser-writing group for integrated quantum photonics, active in 2026 (multi-scan waveguide birefringence preprint with Crespi).

glasses_used: fluoride glasses for mid-IR (research focus of co-worker T. T. Fernandez, Adelaide profile)
topics: Low-loss, low-bend-loss ULI waveguides for 3D photonic integrated circuits, Waveguides, splitters, interferometers, Bragg gratings, integrated lasers and quantum circuits (MQ publication record), Mid-IR integrated photonics in tailored fluoride glasses
summary: The Macquarie group (Withford, Gross) makes fs-laser-written low-loss waveguides, Bragg gratings, waveguide lasers and quantum circuits in bulk glass. Recent work targets high-index, low-bend-loss composite-morphology waveguides and mid-IR fluoride-glass devices.

pi: Peter R. Herman & Shane M. Eaton
affiliation: University of Toronto, Electrical & Computer Engineering (Herman); CNR-IFN Milan (Eaton, formerly in Herman's group).
topics: High-repetition-rate (MHz) writing and heat accumulation vs thermal diffusion
summary: Herman (Toronto) and his former student Eaton (now CNR-IFN) did foundational work on cumulative-heating waveguide writing at MHz repetition rates, which matters for our 60–1008 kHz CARBIDE.
Thomson's Heriot-Watt group is known for ULI astrophotonics and photonic-lattice experiments (Mukherjee's PhD work).

topics: Ultrafast-laser-driven ion migration for high-index-contrast, low-loss waveguides in multicomponent glasses, Two regimes of migration at high repetition rate: light elements first, then heavy elements, High-index-contrast waveguides in fluoride glasses for mid-IR
summary: Solis's CSIC group, with Toney T. Fernandez, showed that high-repetition-rate fs writing in multicomponent glasses (phosphate, tellurite, fluoroborate) drives element-selective ion migration, giving high index contrast. Fernandez now continues this with the Macquarie group on fluoride glasses for the mid-IR.

topics: fs laser exposure plus chemical etching of fused silica for micro-fluidics and micro-mechanics
summary: Bellouard's group works on fs-laser modification and etching of fused silica for 3D micro-devices more than on waveguides.
